defects.fd per record: WriteBatch opens the log file inside the loop and defers each Close to function return, so a batch holds one open descriptor per record until WriteBatch returns and a large batch can exhaust the process file limit.
defects.attempt lost cancel: attempt discards the cancel function of the timeout context, so the timer and context resources are not released when the attempt returns.
defects.handler gets Background: invoke passes context.Background to the handler instead of the timeout context, so the handler never sees JobTimeout and a slow handler is never cancelled.
defects.backoff unit: backoff converts BackoffMS to a time.Duration without multiplying by time.Millisecond, so the delay is BackoffMS nanoseconds instead of milliseconds.
defects.backoff no cap: backoff has no 30 second ceiling, so from the 16th failed attempt on the delay grows past 30 seconds, and a large BackoffMS overflows the shift.
defects.retry bound off by one: runOne retries while attempt is at most MaxAttempts, so a job with MaxAttempts 3 runs four times in total instead of three.
defects.result log completion order: Add appends records at completion under the lock, so with more than one worker the log lines are in completion order and not in lease order.

decoys.decoy errors.Is: Replacing the == comparison with errors.Is on queue.ErrEmpty changes which lease errors end a worker, because errors.Is matches wrapped errors that == would miss.
decoys.decoy slices.Sorted: Returning slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(...)) instead of a sorted slice built by hand changes FailedJobs for a nil map, which now returns a non-nil empty slice.
decoys.decoy range over int: Replacing the worker loop index with range over r.opts.Workers starts one fewer goroutine when Workers is zero, so Run returns without waiting.
decoys.decoy reordered stats and log: Moving the stats update above r.log.Add in runOne drops the record of every failed attempt, because the stats count reads the record that Add has not stored yet.
